newsitem.title: GREECE: Late buying helps Greek shares rebound 1.08pct.
newsitem.headline: Late buying helps Greek shares rebound 1.08pct.

text.p: Late buying helped Greek shares rebound from earlier weakness on foreign selling which drove the benchmark index below 1,600 points.

Shares shrugged off the cautious sentiment spilled over from the French election outcome, reversing a streak of losing sessions. The market fell in the previous week in reaction to unnerved Greek interbank and forex markets.
Fund managers said stocks were surprisingly strong as market sentiment was not affected by temporary domestic and international developments.

"Investors overcame last week's uncertainty over a blip in interbank rates and turbulence in the forex market as well as the French election jitters with remarkable ease," said Costas Devaris, fund manager at closed-end fund Aeolian Invest .
There was selling pressure in select blue chips by foreign investors which was absorbed by new cash inflows.
"Intense selling pressure from foreign portfolios was comfortably outweighed by fresh capital as well as ploughed back profits," said Devaris.

The market exhibited unexpected resilience and capability to cushion pressure in select blue chips, including Alpha Credit Bank, ErgoBank, Titan Cement and to a lesser extent Hellenic Bottling, which started in the previous week, he added.
"On many counts, Greek shares have not been in such good shape for a very long time," Devaris said.
The Athens general index firmed 1.08 percent or 17.68 points to 1,652.99 from Friday's 1,635.31 close, bouncing back from a low of 1,596.02 set early in the session.
The market found considerable support in state telecom OTE which added 400 drachmas to 7,200.
Strong performance in state banks such as National, Commercial and National Mortgage more than offset weakness in Alpha Credit and ErgoBank. The banking sub-index rose 0.32 percent.
Industrials were up 0.69 percent with other sectors mixed.
Turnover was healthy at 27.2 billion drachmas on volume of 4.7 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 111 to 104 with 25 shares unchanged on 240 traded.
